news.title: SAMSUNG INNOVATION CAMPUS | WHY THE FUTURE OF INNOVATION DEPENDS ON THOSE WHO TELL IT'S STORY
news.body:
Every day, universities, innovation hubs and startups develop ideas capable of transforming industries and improving lives. Yet many promising innovations never reach the people they are designed to serve, not because they lack technical merit, but because their stories are never told.

In today's digital economy, storytelling has become an essential innovation competency. Communicating ideas clearly, authentically and consistently is no longer the responsibility of marketers alone. It is increasingly a strategic capability for researchers, engineers, entrepreneurs and innovators seeking to translate knowledge into meaningful societal impact.

This perspective emerged during the official launch of the Samsung Innovation Campus (SIC) Kenya Cohort on 8th July 2026, where participants explored the growing relationship between technology, creativity and digital storytelling.

Reflecting on this intersection, Dr. Lawrence Nderu, Founder of JHUB Africa, challenged participants to view content creation as more than producing material for social media. He emphasized that innovators have a responsibility to document their work, communicate research and make emerging technologies accessible to wider audiences. Research creates knowledge, but storytelling enables that knowledge to inspire collaboration, attract partnerships and accelerate adoption.

This philosophy was reinforced by Edwin Waweru from Samsung Electronics East Africa, Wildlife and Humanitarian Photographer and Digital Content Strategist, whose work demonstrates that photography is far more than capturing images. It documents progress, preserves history and gives innovation a human story that people can understand and connect with.

Perhaps the day's most practical lesson came from Julius "Wololo TV", who challenged participants to abandon the pursuit of perfection before creating. He encouraged aspiring creators to begin with the tools and skills they already possess, reminding them that progress is achieved through consistency, not perfection. Every piece of content becomes an opportunity to learn, improve and refine one's craft. Waiting for the perfect camera, the perfect setup or the perfect moment often means never starting.

His message serves as an important reminder for today's innovators: ideas hidden in notebooks rarely create impact. Innovation becomes meaningful when it is shared, discussed and continuously refined through engagement with others.

As Artificial Intelligence and digital media continue reshaping how knowledge is created and consumed, content creation is no longer optional, it is part of the innovation process itself. Through the Samsung Innovation Campus, Samsung Electronics East Africa, JKUAT and JHUB Africa continue empowering innovators who can not only build transformative solutions, but also tell the stories that inspire communities and shape Africa's digital future.

news.title: SAMSUNG INNOVATION CAMPUS | WHERE INDUSTRY AND ACADEMIA BUILD THE FUTURE TOGETHER
news.body:
Innovation ecosystems thrive when universities and industry move beyond collaboration to co-create opportunities that prepare learners for real-world challenges. As emerging technologies reshape economies, partnerships that combine academic excellence with industry expertise are essential to developing innovators capable of driving sustainable digital transformation.

This vision was reflected during the Samsung Innovation Campus (SIC) Content Creation Masterclass, hosted by JHUB Africa in partnership with Samsung Electronics East Africa on 8th July 2026 at Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology (JKUAT).

The Samsung Innovation Campus is Samsung Electronics' global talent development initiative that equips young people with practical skills in Artificial Intelligence, coding and emerging technologies while connecting classroom learning with industry experience. Beyond technical knowledge, the programme develops critical thinking, creativity and problem-solving to prepare future innovators for the digital economy.

In his opening remarks, Dr. Lawrence Nderu, Founder of JHUB Africa, challenged participants to rethink the purpose of education and innovation. Universities, he noted, must produce solutions not simply graduates. Industry must build innovation ecosystems, not merely products. Students must pursue competence, character and impact alongside technical excellence. His message captured a defining principle: technology transforms society only when capable people are empowered to apply it meaningfully.

That philosophy defines the partnership between Samsung Electronics East Africa, JKUAT and JHUB Africa. By bringing industry closer to academia, Samsung Innovation Campus equips participants with technical expertise, industry exposure and practical perspectives that strengthen their ability to transform ideas into impactful solutions.

Supporting this vision, Nyawira Muraguri highlighted Samsung's commitment to developing future-ready digital talent, while Josphat Ochiel and Ryan Mule demonstrated how resilience, continuous learning and customer-centric innovation translate knowledge into real-world impact.

Through the Samsung Innovation Campus, participants gain more than technical skills. They strengthen their capacity to innovate, communicate ideas effectively, engage with industry and accelerate research translation, entrepreneurship and technology commercialization. As Kenya's digital economy continues to evolve, partnerships such as this are cultivating a new generation of innovators equipped to create lasting societal and economic impact.

news.title: ADVANCING RIGOROUS,PRACTICE-DRIVEN AI IN AFRICA
news.body:
On 9 July 2026, researchers, innovators, entrepreneurs, policymakers, industry leaders, and students convened at African Institute for Capacity Development (AICAD) for Day One of the AI Research Workshop Conference 2026, organized by JHUB Africa and supported through the Legumes Centre of Excellence for Food and Nutrition Security (LCEFoNS).

Held under the theme “Advancing Rigorous Practice-Driven AI in Africa,” the conference created a platform for critical conversations on how African institutions can strengthen AI research, build local capacity, and translate innovation into measurable societal impact.

Opening the workshop, JHUB Africa Founder and Director Dr. Lawrence Nderu challenged participants to move beyond conversations about AI awareness and focus on developing the research, talent, and innovation systems required to position Africa as an active contributor to global AI development. Prof. George Thiong’o, Principal of COPAS, Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology (JKUAT), reinforced the university’s commitment to fostering rigorous, practice-oriented research and innovation.

Throughout the day, speakers explored AI from multiple perspectives.

Samuel Kamochu, Founder and CEO of Meliora Technologies Limited Technologies, reflected on the role of AI in startups, emphasizing that successful innovation begins with solving real problems rather than building technology for its own sake. Dr. Samuel (Maina) Chege, PhD of Microsoft examined the journey from AI research to responsible real-world impact, highlighting the importance of trust, scalability, and translating research outputs into deployable systems.

Participants also engaged with presentations on AI in education, AI-enabled food systems research, data-driven decision-making, responsible innovation, and the practical realities of deploying AI solutions within African contexts. Discussions repeatedly returned to the importance of high-quality data, interdisciplinary collaboration, local relevance, and responsible AI governance.

A recurring message emerged across presentations and audience discussions: Africa’s AI future will not be defined by access to technology alone, but by the continent’s ability to produce rigorous research, build trusted systems, and apply AI to challenges that matter to African communities.

As Day One concluded, the workshop reinforced the value of bringing together academia, industry, innovators, and policymakers to shape a more collaborative and impact-driven AI ecosystem for Africa.
